In the matter of an application under Section 173 of the
 Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
 1.Mamata Palai
 2.Sushree Priyadarsini
 Palai
 3.Sonali Priyadarsini
 Palai .... Appellants
 -versus-
 1.Sudhir Das
 2.D.M., New India
 Assurance Co. Ltd. .... Respondents
For Appellants : Mr. N. Lenka, Advocate For Respondents : Mr. P.K. Mahali, Advocate (R-2)
Coram: Justice V. Narasingh Date of hearing : 05.08.2025 Date of Judgment : 05.08.2025 V.
Narasingh, J. I.A No.93 of 2010
1.
This application has been filed at the instance of Appellants-Claimants seeking condonation of delay of 67 days in preferring this MACA.
2. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering the recitals in the I.A, the delay in filing the appeal is condoned.
3. I.A is accordingly disposed of.
(V. Narasingh) Judge 1.
Mr. P.K. Mahali, learned counsel has entered appearance on behalf of the Insurance Company by filing Vakalatanama in Court.

The same is taken on record.
2.
Heard learned counsel for the Appellants- Claimants and learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

3. The Appellants-Claimants assailing the judgment dated 3.2.2009 passed by the learned 1st Mamata Palai vs Sudhir Das on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45485011/
1 M.A.C.T, Cuttack in Misc. Case No.481 of 2002 awarding a compensation of Rs.5,21,500/- to the Claimants with interest at the rate of 7.5 % per annum have filed this appeal, seeking enhancement of the compensation amount.

4. The Appellants as Claimants filed the aforesaid M.A.C Case claiming compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- on account of the death of the deceased Gopabandhu Palai in a vehicular accident involving Hero Honda Splendor Motor Cycle bearing registration number OR-05-L-7800 and one Auto Rickshaw bearing registration number OR-05-K- 1471.
In such claim application, the owner of the offending truck was set ex parte.
Respondent No.2- Insurance Company appeared and filed its written statement opposing the claim.
5. On the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed;

" 1. Whether due to rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the vehicle bearing registration number OR-05-K-1471 (Dala Auto) the accident took place and in that accident, one Gopabandhu Palai succumbed to the injuries ?

2. Whether the petitioner(s) is/are entitled to get compensation ? if so what would be the extent ?
3. Whether all the Opp. Parties or any of the Opp. Parties are/is liable to pay compensation ?
4.
To what relief, if any, the petitioner(s) is/are entitled to ?"

In order to substantiate their stand, Claimant No.1 examined herself as P.W.1 and two independent witnesses examined as P.Ws.2 and 3 and documents were exhibited and marked as Exts.1 to 15.
Neither oral nor documentary evidence was adduced on behalf of the Insurance Company
On consideration of the materials on record, learned Tribunal directed for compensation of Rs.5,21,500/- along with interest at the rate of 7.5% from 17.7.2022 till realization.

6. To substantiate its claim for enhancement, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the Claimants that the learned Tribunal has committed a patent error in quantifying the income disregarding the testimony of P.W.1 widow that her husband was getting a sum of Rs.12,000/- per month from the cloth store in the name and style M/s. Haramani Cloth Store.
It is apt to note that P.W.3 who claimed to be an employee under the deceased has stated that his income to be Rs.5000/-.
Referring to the same, it submitted by the learned counsel that the monthly income of the deceased ought to have been construed as Rs.5000/-.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company referred to the contradictions in the testimony of P.W.1, the widow and P.W.3 regarding monthly income from the cloth store.

Hence, it Mamata Palai vs Sudhir Das on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45485011/
2 is submitted that there is no infirmity in the order of the learned Tribunal arriving at a conclusion that monthly income of the deceased would be Rs.4000/-.

entities.text:
Mamata Palai vs Sudhir Das on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45485011/
2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As noted above, evidence of P.W.3 that he was getting Rs.5000/- working in the cloth store of the deceased had stood the test of cross-examination.

8. Hence, on a conspectus of the evidence on record, this Court is of the considered view that assessing the compensation taking into account the income as Rs.5000/- per month would subserve the ends of justice, on the touch stone of the doctrine of just compensation.
9. It is the further contention of the learned counsel for the Claimants that no amount has been awarded on account of general damages.

10. Quantifying the compensation taking annual income to Rs.5000/- and deducting 2/3rd towards personal expenses and taking the multiplier as '16' as fixed by the learned Tribunal, the compensation comes to Rs.6,40,000/- and in addition to the general damages of Rs.9,500/-, the same comes to Rs.6,49,500/-.
There is no dispute at the Bar that an amount of Rs.5,21,000/- along with interest at the rate of 7.5% from 17.7.2002 in terms of the impugned award has already been paid.
Thus balance amount comes to Rs.1,18,500/-.
So applying the doctrine of just compensation the enhanced amount is quantified as Rs.1,30,000/- on consolidated basis.
Accordingly, this Court directs the Insurance Company to pay a further consolidated sum of Rs.1,30,000/- to the Claimants within a period of eight weeks hence.
Considering the age of the Claimant No.1, the widow, such amount be disbursed to her.

Court fees shall be payable by the Claimants as per Rules.
11.
Accordingly, the MACA stands disposed of.
No costs.
(V. Narasingh) Judge Orissa High Court, Cuttack Dated the 05th August, 2025/
Pradeep
